chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about a man who marries a woman and also marries the mother of his (the woman's) Umm al-Walad (concubine/mother of child), so he said, 'There is no harm in that.'

key_terms.أُمَّ وَلَدٍ: Umm al-Walad: A female slave from whom her master has had a child; she becomes free upon his death and cannot be sold.
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: La ba'sa: There is no harm; a phrase indicating permissibility or lack of prohibition.

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible in Shia fiqh to marry a woman and her mother if the mother is a concubine?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the permissibility of *Jam' al-Ustadhain* (marrying two sisters or a woman and her mother) specifically when the mother is an *Umm al-Walad* (concubine with whom the master has had a child), distinguishing it from the general prohibition of marrying two sisters simultaneously. Shaykh al-Tusi includes this in the chapter on concubinage to highlight the unique status of *Umm al-Walad*, whose marriage to her master is treated with the same legal weight as a free wife regarding prohibitions of kinship. This ruling underscores the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding marital unions within the same family line under specific conditions of concubinage.
